deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This folio is working material for Riemann's 1860 paper 'Ueber die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 8). The previous page set up a Green/Riemann-function argument for a model hyperbolic equation. This page carries the whole programme for the gas-dynamic case. The next page finishes the Riemann function as a Gauss hypergeometric function.

(A) Equations of motion (top left). Euler and continuity equations for 1-D isentropic flow:
- (1/rho) dp/dx = -u_t - u u_x
- rho_t + (rho u)_x = 0
The boxed side computation derives Poisson's adiabatic law. Start from p = a^2 rho sigma (sigma ~ temperature) and dQ = A drho + B dsigma, and set dQ = 0. This gives (k-1) drho/rho = dsigma/sigma, so sigma = C rho^(k-1) and p = a^2 rho^k. Routine.

(B) Riemann invariants. Put s = log rho. The momentum equation becomes a^2 k e^{(k-1)s} s_x = -u_t - u u_x, and continuity becomes u_x = -s_t - u s_x.
- Define phi'(s) = a sqrt(k) e^{(k-1)s/2} = sqrt(dp/drho), the sound speed c.
- Then phi(s) = (2a sqrt(k)/(k-1)) e^{(k-1)s/2}, i.e. phi = 2c/(k-1).
- Multiply continuity by phi' and add or subtract the momentum equation (implicit step, mine). With 2p = u + phi and 2q = phi - u (the letters p, q now denote the invariants, not pressure), this gives:
  - p_t = -(u + phi') p_x
  - q_t = -(u - phi') q_x
These are Riemann's invariants r, s of the 1860 paper. Inversion relations: u = p - q, phi = p + q, phi' s_p = phi' s_q = 1, and d log phi'/ds = (k-1)/2, so phi' = ((k-1)/2)(p+q).

(C) Hodograph transformation. Take x, t as functions of (p,q). p is constant along dx/dt = u + phi', so:
- x_q = (u + phi') t_q
- x_p = (u - phi') t_p
Cross-differentiating gives 2 phi' t_pq + t_q (1 + phi'' s_p) + t_p (1 + phi'' s_q) = 0. Riemann first wrote this line, then struck it. Since phi'' s_p = (k-1)/2, the equation reduces to (4 phi'/(k+1)) t_pq + t_p + t_q = 0, i.e.
  2((k-1)/(k+1)) (p+q) t_pq + t_p + t_q = 0,
an Euler–Poisson–Darboux (EPD) equation.

(D) Potential w. Riemann introduces dw = (x - (u+phi')t) dp - (x - (u-phi')t) dq. The form is exact because x_q = (u+phi') t_q and x_p = (u-phi') t_p. Hence w_p + w_q = ∓2 phi' t, and w_pq is a constant multiple of t. Eliminating t gives a second-order EPD equation for w. On the page he writes it as 2((k-1)/(k+1)) (p+q) w_pq + w_p + w_q = 0, the same form as the t-equation (see errors).

(E) Riemann's method (Green identity with the adjoint). Write c = 2(k-1)/(k+1). Then
  ∬ (c(p+q) w_pq + w_p + w_q) v dp dq = ∬ (c ((p+q)v)_pq - v_p - v_q) w dp dq + boundary integral.
The Riemann function v must:
- solve the adjoint equation c((p+q)v)_pq - v_p - v_q = 0;
- satisfy c((p+q)v)_q - v = 0 on p = p' and c((p+q)v)_p - v = 0 on q = q';
- equal 1 at (p',q').
On p = p' the condition is c(p+q) v_q + ((k-3)/(k+1)) v = 0. Integrating gives v = C (p+q)^{-(k-3)/(2(k-1))} = C (p+q)^{-1/2 + 1/(k-1)}. The same holds on q = q'.

(F) Separation of variables in sigma = p+q, u = p-q. Here ∂_p + ∂_q = 2∂_sigma and ∂_p∂_q = ∂_sigma^2 - ∂_u^2.
- The adjoint becomes sigma(v_ss - v_uu) + ((k-3)/(k-1)) v_s = 0.
- Try v = e^{mu u} Σ a_n sigma^n. This gives Σ a_n n(n-1+b) sigma^{n-1} = mu^2 Σ a_n sigma^{n+1}.
- The even coefficients are a_{2n} = C (mu/2)^{2n}/(n! Π(n+nu)) with 2nu = b-1. For the adjoint, nu = -1/(k-1), giving Riemann's Π(n - 1/(k-1)). These are modified-Bessel series sigma^{-nu} I_nu(mu sigma).
- He replaces 1/Π(n-nu) by a Hankel-type loop integral ∫ e^x x^{-n+nu-1} dx (the constant 2πi is suppressed). Summing gives ∫ e^{x + (sigma mu)^2/(4x)} x^{1/(k-1)-1} dx, a Schläfli-type Bessel integral.
- Rescaling x -> (sigma mu/2) x and using mu u + (mu sigma/2)(x + 1/x) = (mu/2)(p(x+1)^2/x + q(x-1)^2/x) gives the integrand.
- Superposing over mu gives v = (p+q)^{1/(k-1)} ∫ f(p(x+1)^2/x + q(x-1)^2/x) x^{1/(k-1)-1} dx with f arbitrary.

(G) Choosing homogeneous f. The quadratic p(x+1)^2 + q(x-1)^2 = (p+q)(x^2 + 2cos2phi x + 1), where cos 2phi = (p-q)/(p+q). Its roots are expressed via sqrt(q) + i sqrt(p) = r e^{i phi}, giving roots -e^{±2i phi}; Riemann normalises the sign into x.
- With f = z^{-1/(k-1)}, the integral becomes an Euler integral of the form ∫ (x - e^{2i phi})^{-λ} (1 - x e^{-2i phi})^{-λ} x^{...} dx.
- With f = z^{-1/2}, the prefactor is (p+q)^{-1/2+1/(k-1)}, which matches the characteristic boundary condition of (E). This gives
  v = (p+q)^{-1/2+1/(k-1)} ∫ (1 - x e^{-2i phi})^{-1/2} (1 - x e^{2i phi})^{-1/2} x^{1/(k-1)-1/2} dx.
- He identifies this as a Riemann P-function in e^{4 i phi}, with exponent sets drawn from {0, 1/2, 1/(k-1), 1/2 - 1/(k-1)}. This is completed on the next page as F(1/2 + 1/(k-1), 1/2 - 1/(k-1); 1; -(p-p')(q-q')/((p+q)(p'+q'))).

(H) Middle box. An attempt to rationalise via p = x^2, q = y^2 (implicit, mine), z = x + iy, z' = x - iy, so that p + q = z z'. The adjoint operator is rewritten in z, z'. Abandoned.

(I) Fourier–Bessel solution of the Cauchy problem (right side and lower right). For the w-equation sigma(w_ss - w_uu) + ((k+1)/(k-1)) w_s = 0:
- Separated solutions are e^{mu u} f(mu sigma), with f = Σ (sigma mu/2)^{2n}/(n! Π(n + 1/(k-1))), and a second solution phi(mu sigma) from the index -1/(k-1).
- Superpose w = ∫_0^∞ (φ(mu) cos mu u + ψ(mu) sin mu u) f(mu sigma) dmu; this line is struck and replaced by a two-solution form.
- Determine the coefficients from w and w_sigma on sigma = sigma' by Fourier inversion (1/π)∫ w' cos mu u' du'.
- The Wronskian y y1' - y1 y' = const·sigma^{-(k+1)/(k-1)} is used to solve the 2x2 system.
- The result is a double integral w = (1/π)∫∫ cos mu(u-u') (mu sigma')^{(k+1)/(k-1)} [w'(φ f - f φ) - (∂w'/∂sigma')(...)/mu] dmu du'. This is the alternative route that the Riemann-function method of (E)–(G) replaces.
errors: In (D) the derivative is mis-evaluated. With u = p-q and phi' = ((k-1)/2)(p+q), one has ∂(u+phi')/∂q = -1 + (k-1)/2 = (k-3)/2, so ∂(x-(u+phi')t)/∂q = -t(k-3)/2 = t(3-k)/2. Riemann writes t(k+1)/2, and symmetrically -t(k+1)/2 for the p-derivative, which is consistent with a sign slip in ∂u/∂q or ∂phi'/∂q. Exactness still holds, but the resulting w-equation on this page coincides with the t-equation, coefficient (k+1)/(2(k-1)). With the correct value, w satisfies w_pq - ((k-3)/(2(k-1)(p+q)))(w_p+w_q) = 0.
Mitigating point for the slip above: the next page's hypergeometric parameters 1/2 ± 1/(k-1) are symmetric under beta -> 1-beta. So the final Riemann function is unaffected up to the power prefactor.
The sign in 'w_p + w_q = 2phi' t' should be -2phi' t for dw as written (P + Q = -2 phi' t).
The Hankel-type representation 1/Π(n-nu) = ∫ e^x x^{-n+nu-1} dx omits the factor 1/(2πi) and does not specify the contour. This is harmless, being absorbed into 'Const.'.
The x-exponent in the first P-function integral (transcribed x^{-1}) appears inconsistent with x^{1/(k-1)-1}·x^{1/(k-1)} = x^{2/(k-1)-1}. This is either a slip or a misreading.

Invariants 2p = u + phi(s), 2q = phi(s) - u with phi = 2c/(k-1), transported along dx/dt = u ± c
results.modern_name: Riemann invariants / characteristics of 1-D isentropic gas dynamics

results.what: Interchange of dependent and independent variables giving a linear EPD equation for t(p,q)

Separated solutions e^{mu u} sigma^{-nu} I_nu(mu sigma) and their Schläfli/Hankel loop-integral representation
results.modern_name: Modified Bessel functions; Schläfli integral; Hankel contour for 1/Gamma

results.what: Riemann function expressed as a Riemann P-function / Gauss hypergeometric function
results.modern_name: Riemann function of the EPD equation, F(beta, 1-beta; 1; z)

results.modern_name: Hankel/Fourier transform solution of the EPD equation

deep.surprise_reason: This is draft work for Riemann's published 1860 shock-wave paper: invariants, hodograph, Riemann function, hypergeometric solution. The only mildly notable unpublished details are the abandoned Fourier–Bessel route and the use of a Schläfli-type Bessel integral and Hankel-type loop integral before Hankel/Schläfli published them. Riemann already used the loop integral for Gamma in 1859.

transcription_corrections: '4φ(s)/(k+1) ∂²t/∂p∂q' should read 4φ'(s)/(k+1), since 4φ'/(k+1) = 2(k-1)(p+q)/(k+1), as the w-line itself confirms.
In the lower series line 'n(n-1) - (k+1)/(k-1)' should be n(n-1+(k+1)/(k-1)).
'√p + √q i = re^{φi}' is probably √q + √p i = re^{φi}, giving e^{2φi} = (√q+i√p)²/(p+q).
In the line beginning (k-1)/(k+1)(∂²v/∂σ² - σ ∂²v/∂ω²), ω should be u, and the first term carries σ as well: σ(v_σσ - v_uu).
'a_n ... = Const.' refers to the even coefficients a_{2n}.
In the boundary integral 'w(w + 2(k-1)/(k+1)…)dp' the first factor is v: v(w + c(p+q) ∂w/∂p) dp.
